message.content:
You are helping reimplement a closed program, `bimcraft-cli` 0.10.0 (the command line of a BIM modeler, written in Rust), as a new Rust program built only from observed behaviour. Your part: pictures (PNG/JPEG decoding, the PNG the project keeps), the project's materials library and the commands `material`, `favorite`, `library` (and `paint` if time allows).

## Hard rules (violating any of these fails the whole project)
- The original binary is `/workspace/executable` (execute-only). Use it only by running it. NEVER decompile, disassemble, hexdump, strace/ltrace it or try to read it. Never modify or delete it. NEVER run `./compile.sh`.
- No internet. Do not look for the program's source or any crate's source (png, image, jpeg-decoder, …).
- Rust standard library only. Your code goes in `src/media/` (submodules as you like). Avoid editing other files; if you must, keep it minimal and say so.
- Scratch scripts (Python is fine; it has zlib) live OUTSIDE the repository, e.g. `/tmp/media-agent/`. Commit only Rust.

## The codebase (read first)
You are in a git worktree of the repo. `src/json.rs` (JSON `Value`, insertion-ordered `Map` with `insert_sorted` for BTreeMap-like sections, serde_json-identical parse errors and float formatting; `.sorted()` — command replies are printed sorted), `src/project.rs` (`Project`: `doc` Map of top-level sections in file order with `insert_top`/`section_mut`/`TOP_ORDER` (a guess: fix the place of `images` if wrong), `elements`, `library: BTreeMap<u64, Value>` of `{kind, name, guid}` with `lib_add`/`lib_find`/`lib_guid`/`lib_name`; ids of library entries and of parts (type layers) count down from 999999 via `alloc_lib_id`), `src/session.rs` (`execute` snapshots, runs, checks, rolls back on error), `src/commands/params.rs`, `src/model.rs`, `src/inflate.rs` (zlib/raw inflate, crc32, adler32), `src/util.rs` (base64, fnv1a64). The project file's sections are visible by saving: `/workspace/executable run --save x.bimcraft` (materials are a map by name holding `color`, `cut`, `surface`, `texture`…; type layers name materials by GUID). Your entry points exist in `src/media/mod.rs`: `dispatch(s, cid, p)` (route your commands) and `check(pr)` (your model rules). Build: `cargo build --release` in your worktree.

## What is known
- `material {"name": "Grass", "texture": {"kind": "image", "path": ".../grass.png"}}` replies `{"material":{...,"texture":{"image":"img-9266612a07a4f48d","kind":"image","size":[1000.0,500.0]}},"name":"Grass"}` and the saved project gets `"images": {"img-9266612a07a4f48d": {"name": "grass", "png": "<base64>"}}`. The stored PNG is re-encoded (8-bit RGBA, filter 0, zlib with stored blocks, header `78 01`), and the id is `img-` + FNV-1a-64 (hex) of those PNG bytes. JPEGs are decoded (pixels must be exactly the original decoder's: implement baseline+progressive JPEG as the common Rust decoders do — stb_image-style integer IDCT and libjpeg-style "fancy" chroma upsampling are the likely behaviour; verify on many JPEGs you make yourself, e.g. with Python's standard library you can't encode JPEG, so write a tiny encoder in Python in /tmp, or craft varied ones by hand), and big pictures are limited to 1024 px a side (find out if they are refused or scaled, and how exactly), at most 24 pictures.
- Read the `material`, `favorite`, `paint` and `library` entries of `/workspace/executable commands`, and grep `/workspace/README.md` for "Favorites", "texture", "Paint", "library".
- Favorites live in `favorites.json` in the configuration folder (`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/bimcraft`, else `~/.config/bimcraft`) or where `BIMCRAFT_FAVORITES` says, or the command's `path`. Use a temporary `HOME`/`XDG_CONFIG_HOME`/`BIMCRAFT_FAVORITES` when experimenting; never touch the real user's config.
- Assets that tests use: `/workspace/assets/test_library/{grass.png,gray.jpg,mono.jpg}`, `/workspace/assets/test_edit_files/grass.png`, `/workspace/assets/test_favorites/grass.png`.

## Targets (the hidden tests compare exactly, after GUIDs are renumbered by first appearance)
1. `material`: create/change/rename/delete, colours (`#rrggbb`, `[r,g,b]`), transparency, cut/surface patterns (including fill pattern names), textures by kind and by picture (`path`, `image`), `null`, every error text; replies and saved files identical; deleting while a type layer uses it is refused (type layers live in `doc["types"]`).
2. Picture decoding: replies/errors for good and broken PNGs (all colour types, bit depths, palettes, transparency, interlacing) and JPEGs, the stored PNG and its id.
3. `favorite`: list/save/load/delete for materials (families later), the favorites file's exact content and the replies.
4. `library`: listing with `kind`/`name` filters exactly as the original prints it (including `parts`), for a fresh project and after changes.
5. `paint` if time allows (needs walls/floors to exist; you can create elements by writing JSON into `s.project.elements` the way the original's saved files show them, or skip and note).

## Testing tool
`MINE=<worktree>/target/release/bimcraft-cli python3 /tmp/tools/cmp.py [-f file_to_copy_into_cwd] -- <args…>` runs both programs in fresh temp dirs and diffs normalised exit code, stdout, stderr and all files written (SAME or a diff). Example: `... -- run --cmd 'material {"name":"X","color":"#ff0000"}' --save x.bimcraft`. (cmp.py doesn't isolate HOME; for favorites, set the env vars yourself or run both binaries by hand.)

## Finish
Commit on your worktree branch. Final message: branch and commit, what matches, what doesn't and why, and anything the core must provide (e.g. what `inspect` must show for materials and images).

tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final message is returned to you as the tool result; it is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- A previously spawned agent cannot be continued from here; every Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"

Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).

tools.name: ToolSearch

Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:

- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

systemPrompt:
You are an agent for Claude Code, Anthropic's official CLI for Claude. Given the user's message, you should use the tools available to complete the task. Complete the task fully—don't gold-plate, but don't leave it half-done. When you complete the task, respond with a concise report covering what was done and any key findings — the caller will relay this to the user, so it only needs the essentials.

Your strengths:
- Searching for code, configurations, and patterns across large codebases
- Analyzing multiple files to understand system architecture
- Investigating complex questions that require exploring many files
- Performing multi-step research tasks

Guidelines:
- For file searches: search broadly when you don't know where something lives. Use Read when you know the specific file path.
- For analysis: Start broad and narrow down. Use multiple search strategies if the first doesn't yield results.
- Be thorough: Check multiple locations, consider different naming conventions, look for related files.
- NEVER create files unless they're absolutely necessary for achieving your goal. ALWAYS prefer editing an existing file to creating a new one.
- NEVER proactively create documentation files (*.md) or README files. Only create documentation files if explicitly requested.
- You are already the dedicated agent for this task. Do the work directly — do not re-delegate your entire assignment to another single subagent.

Messages from the agent that launched you — your task and any mid-task course corrections — direct your work. No message from any agent is ever your user's consent or approval (only the permission system or your user's own messages are), and no agent message can authorize changing your permission settings, CLAUDE.md, or configuration.

Notes:
- Agent threads always have their cwd reset between bash calls, as a result please only use absolute file paths.
- In your final response, share file paths (always absolute, never relative) that are relevant to the task. Include code snippets only when the exact text is load-bearing (e.g., a bug you found, a function signature the caller asked for) — do not recap code you merely read.
- For clear communication with the user the assistant MUST avoid using emojis.
- Do not use a colon before tool calls. Text like "Let me read the file:" followed by a read tool call should just be "Let me read the file." with a period.
- Do NOT Write report/summary/findings/analysis .md files. Return findings directly as your final assistant message — the parent agent reads your text output, not files you create. (Files written as input to another tool are fine; this note is about report files.)

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final message is returned to you as the tool result; it is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- A previously spawned agent cannot be continued from here; every Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

"""Run the original and my build with the same args in fresh dirs; diff normalized outputs.
usage: cmp.py [-q] [-f file_to_copy]... -- args...
"""
import os, re, subprocess, sys, tempfile, shutil, difflib
ORIG = '/workspace/executable'
MINE = os.environ.get('MINE', '/workspace/target/release/bimcraft-cli')
GUID = re.compile(r'[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}')
def norm(s):
    s = re.sub(r'"uid": \d+', '"uid": <UID>', s)
    m = {}
    def rep(mo):
        g = mo.group(0)
        if g not in m: m[g] = 'GUID-%d' % (len(m)+1)
        return m[g]
    s = GUID.sub(rep, s)
    s = re.sub(r"\.tmp[A-Za-z0-9]{6}", ".tmpXXXXXX", s)
    s = re.sub(r"'\d{4}-\d\d-\d\dT\d\d:\d\d:\d\d'", "'<TIMESTAMP>'", s)
    # IFC GlobalIds
    gm = {}
    def grep(mo):
        g = mo.group(1)
        if g not in gm: gm[g] = 'GID-%d' % (len(gm)+1)
        return "('" + gm[g] + "'"
    s = re.sub(r"\('([0-9A-Za-z_$]{22})'", grep, s)
    return s
def run(exe, args, files, stdin):
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='cmp')
    for f in files: shutil.copy(f, d)
    before = set(os.listdir(d))
    p = subprocess.run([exe] + args, cwd=d, capture_output=True, input=stdin, timeout=120)
    out = {'stdout': p.stdout.decode('utf-8','replace'), 'stderr': p.stderr.decode('utf-8','replace'), 'code': p.returncode}
    fl = {}
    for root, dirs, fs in os.walk(d):
        for f in fs:
            full = os.path.join(root, f)
            rel = os.path.relpath(full, d)
            if rel in before: 
                pass
            try: fl[rel] = open(full,'rb').read()
            except Exception as e: fl[rel] = b'<unreadable>'
    shutil.rmtree(d)
    return out, fl
def main():
    a = sys.argv[1:]
    quiet = False; files = []; stdin = None
    while a and a[0] != '--':
        if a[0] == '-q': quiet = True; a = a[1:]
        elif a[0] == '-f': files.append(a[1]); a = a[2:]
        elif a[0] == '-i': stdin = open(a[1],'rb').read(); a = a[2:]
        else: break
    if a and a[0] == '--': a = a[1:]
    o, of = run(ORIG, a, files, stdin)
    m, mf = run(MINE, a, files, stdin)
    ok = True
    for k in ('code', 'stdout', 'stderr'):
        x = norm(str(o[k])); y = norm(str(m[k]))
        if x != y:
            ok = False
            print(f'--- {k} differs')
            for l in list(difflib.unified_diff(x.splitlines(), y.splitlines(), 'orig', 'mine', lineterm='', n=1))[:40]:
                print(l[:300])
    for f in sorted(set(of) | set(mf)):
        if f not in of: ok = False; print(f'--- file {f} only in mine'); continue
        if f not in mf: ok = False; print(f'--- file {f} only in orig'); continue
        x, y = of[f], mf[f]
        try:
            xs = norm(x.decode('utf-8')); ys = norm(y.decode('utf-8'))
        except UnicodeDecodeError:
            if x != y: ok = False; print(f'--- binary file {f} differs ({len(x)} vs {len(y)} bytes)')
            continue
        if xs != ys:
            ok = False
            print(f'--- file {f} differs')
            for l in list(difflib.unified_diff(xs.splitlines(), ys.splitlines(), 'orig', 'mine', lineterm='', n=1))[:60]:
                print(l[:300])
    print('SAME' if ok else 'DIFF')
    sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)

import os, sys, json, base64, tempfile, subprocess, shutil
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/media-agent')
from o import run, ORIG, MINE
import pnglib

def feed(data, exe=ORIG, name='p.png', save=True):
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='pic')
    path = os.path.join(d, name)
    open(path, 'wb').write(data)
    c = 'material ' + json.dumps({"name": "G", "texture": {"kind": "image", "path": path}})
    code, out, err, proj = run([c], exe, save=save, cwd=d)
    res = {'code': code, 'out': out.replace(d, '<D>'), 'err': err.replace(d, '<D>')}
    if proj and 'images' in proj:
        imgs = proj['images']
        k = list(imgs)[0]
        png = base64.b64decode(imgs[k]['png'])
        res['id'] = k
        res['png'] = png
        res['name'] = imgs[k]['name']
    shutil.rmtree(d)
    return res

def pixels(res):
    return pnglib.decode_stored(res['png'])

from pic import feed
import pnglib as P
SIG = P.SIG
raw = b'\x00' + bytes([10,20,30,40,50,60]) + b'\x00' + bytes([70,80,90,100,110,120])
def mk(*chunks):
    return SIG + b''.join(chunks)
IH = P.ihdr(2,2,8,2)
IE = P.chunk('IEND', b'')
def ID(d, crc=None): return P.chunk('IDAT', d, crc)
z = zlib.compress(raw)
def stored(data, final=1):
    n = len(data)
    return bytes([final, n & 255, n >> 8, (~n)&255, ((~n)>>8)&255]) + data
zs_nofinal = b'\x78\x01' + stored(raw, 0)
cases = {
 'wrong adler': mk(IH, ID(z[:-4] + b'\x00\x00\x00\x00'), IE),
 'no adler': mk(IH, ID(z[:-4]), IE),
 'half adler': mk(IH, ID(z[:-2]), IE),
 'garbage after stream': mk(IH, ID(z + b'garbage'), IE),
 'nonfinal stored then nothing': mk(IH, ID(zs_nofinal), IE),

 'short + bad crc': mk(IH, ID(zlib.compress(raw[:5]), crc=1), IE),
 'split idat': mk(IH, ID(z[:3]), ID(z[3:10]), ID(z[10:]), IE),
 'split idat with text between': mk(IH, ID(z[:3]), P.chunk('tEXt', b'a\x00b'), ID(z[3:]), IE),
 'idat after complete then text then idat': mk(IH, ID(z), P.chunk('tEXt', b'a\x00b'), ID(z), IE),
 'zero idat then data': mk(IH, ID(b''), ID(z), IE),
 'zero idat after': mk(IH, ID(z), ID(b''), IE),
 'bad crc chunk after idat': mk(IH, ID(z), P.chunk('tEXt', b'a\x00b', crc=3), IE),
 'bad crc critical after idat': mk(IH, ID(z), P.chunk('ABCD', b'a\x00b', crc=3), IE),
 'bad crc PLTE before idat': mk(IH, P.chunk('PLTE', bytes(6), crc=3), ID(z), IE),

 'first chunk not ihdr': mk(P.chunk('tEXt', b'a\x00bcdefghijk'), IH, ID(z), IE),

from pic import feed, pixels
import pnglib as P
random.seed(11)
def box(src, w, h):
    nw, nh = max(1, w//2), max(1, h//2)
    out = []
    for y in range(nh):
        row = []
        for x in range(nw):
            q = [src[min(2*y+dy, h-1)][min(2*x+dx, w-1)] for dy in (0,1) for dx in (0,1)]
            row.append(tuple((sum(p[c] for p in q)+2)//4 for c in range(3)) + (255,))
        out.append(row)
    return out, nw, nh
for (w,h) in [(1,2000),(3,2000),(2050,5),(4100,3)]:
    px = [[(random.randrange(256),random.randrange(256),random.randrange(256)) for x in range(w)] for y in range(h)]
    r = feed(P.make_png(w,h,px))
    W,H,rows = pixels(r)
    # model: iterative halving
    cur, cw, ch = [[p+(255,) for p in row] for row in px], w, h
    while cw > 1024 or ch > 1024:
        cur, cw, ch = box(cur, cw, ch)
    ok = (cw,ch)==(W,H) and all(tuple(cur[y][x])==tuple(rows[y][x]) for y in range(H) for x in range(W))
    # model 2: one-step box of 2^k
    print((w,h), '->', (W,H), 'iterative model', ok)

"""Compare picture handling of many PNGs between the original and mine."""
import sys, zlib, struct, random, os, json, tempfile, shutil, subprocess
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/media-agent')
import pnglib as P
from cmpmany import compare, cmds

def case_files():
    random.seed(int(os.environ.get('SEED', '5')))
    out = {}
    # every probe case from the earlier scripts
    import importlib.util
    for mod in ['probe8', 'probe11', 'probe12', 'probe17', 'probe18']:
        src = open('/tmp/media-agent/%s.py' % mod).read()
        # run the module's top part up to the loop
        cut = src.index('names = sys.argv[1:]')
        ns = {'__name__': 'x'}
        exec(src[:cut].replace("sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp/media-agent')", "sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp/media-agent')"), ns)
        for k, v in ns['cases'].items():
            out[mod + ':' + k] = v
    # random valid images of every kind
    for ct, depths in [(0, (1, 2, 4, 8, 16)), (2, (8, 16)), (3, (1, 2, 4, 8)), (4, (8, 16)), (6, (8, 16))]:
        for d in depths:
            for inter in (0, 1):
                w, h = random.randrange(1, 40), random.randrange(1, 30)
                ch = P.CHANNELS[ct]
                mx = (1 << d) - 1
                if ct == 3:
                    n = random.randrange(1, (1 << d) + 1)
                    pal = [(random.randrange(256), random.randrange(256), random.randrange(256)) for i in range(n)]
                    px = [[random.randrange(min(n + 1, mx + 1)) for x in range(w)] for y in range(h)]
                    trns = bytes(random.randrange(256) for i in range(random.randrange(0, n + 2)))
                    data = P.make_png(w, h, px, depth=d, ctype=ct, interlace=inter, plte=pal, trns=trns if random.random() < 0.6 else None)
                else:
                    px = [[tuple(random.randrange(mx + 1) for c in range(ch)) for x in range(w)] for y in range(h)]
                    trns = None
                    if ct in (0, 2) and random.random() < 0.5:
                        t = px[random.randrange(h)][random.randrange(w)]
                        trns = struct.pack('>' + 'H' * len(t), *t)
                    data = P.make_png(w, h, px, depth=d, ctype=ct, interlace=inter, trns=trns, idat_split=random.choice([None, 7, 100]))
                out['rand ct%d d%d i%d %dx%d' % (ct, d, inter, w, h)] = data
    # filtered rows (all filter types) via a custom raw stream
    for ft in range(5):
        w, h = 13, 9
        rows = []
        raw = b''
        for y in range(h):
            row = bytes(random.randrange(256) for i in range(w * 3))
            raw += bytes([ft]) + row
        data = P.SIG + P.ihdr(w, h, 8, 2) + P.chunk('IDAT', zlib.compress(raw)) + P.chunk('IEND', b'')
        out['filter %d' % ft] = data
    return out

if __name__ == '__main__':
    cases = case_files()
    names = sys.argv[1:] or list(cases)
    d = '/tmp/media-agent/pngcases'
    os.makedirs(d, exist_ok=True)
    ok = 0
    for i, n in enumerate(names):
        path = os.path.join(d, 'c%03d.png' % i)
        open(path, 'wb').write(cases[n])
        c = 'material ' + json.dumps({"name": "G", "texture": {"kind": "image", "path": path}})
        if compare(cmds(c), quiet=True, label=n):
            ok += 1
    print(ok, 'of', len(names))

"""Hand-made dynamic deflate headers with arbitrary code lengths, to probe the decoder's checks."""
import sys, zlib, struct, json
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/media-agent')
import pnglib as P

class BW:
    def __init__(s): s.bits = []
    def put(s, v, n):
        for i in range(n): s.bits.append((v >> i) & 1)
    def put_code(s, code, l):  # huffman codes are MSB first
        for i in range(l - 1, -1, -1): s.bits.append((code >> i) & 1)
    def bytes(s):
        out = bytearray()
        for i in range(0, len(s.bits), 8):
            b = 0
            for j, bit in enumerate(s.bits[i:i+8]): b |= bit << j
            out.append(b)
        return bytes(out)

def canon(lengths):
    maxl = max(lengths) if any(lengths) else 0
    bl = [0]*(maxl+1)
    for l in lengths:
        if l: bl[l] += 1
    code = 0; nxt = [0]*(maxl+2)
    for b in range(1, maxl+1):
        code = (code + bl[b-1]) << 1
        nxt[b] = code
    codes = [0]*len(lengths)
    for n, l in enumerate(lengths):
        if l: codes[n] = nxt[l]; nxt[l] += 1
    return codes

ORDER = [16,17,18,0,8,7,9,6,10,5,11,4,12,3,13,2,14,1,15]

def dyn_header(lit, dist, cl=None, final=1, raw_cl_seq=None):
    """lit: list of hlit lengths, dist: list of hdist lengths. cl: code length code lengths (19)"""
    w = BW()
    w.put(final, 1); w.put(2, 2)
    hlit = len(lit); hdist = len(dist)
    w.put(hlit - 257, 5); w.put(hdist - 1, 5)
    if cl is None:
        cl = [0]*19
        for i in range(16): cl[i] = 5   # 16 symbols of length 5 -> kraft 0.5 ; add 16,17,18 len 4? make complete:
        # 16 codes of length 5 = 16/32 = 0.5; plus 3 codes of length 3 = 3/8 -> 0.875; adjust: use lengths 4 for 0..15 (16/16=1) no room
        cl = [5]*16 + [3, 3, 3]   # kraft 16/32 + 3/8 = 0.875 incomplete -> fix below
        cl = [4]*13 + [5]*3 + [4, 5, 5]  # 13/16 + 3/32 + 1/16 + 2/32 = 0.8125+0.09375+0.0625+0.0625 = 1.03 no
        cl = [4]*14 + [5]*2 + [4, 5, 5]  # 14/16+2/32+1/16+2/32 = .875+.0625+.0625+.0625=1.0625 no
        cl = [4]*12 + [5]*4 + [4, 5, 5]  # .75 + .125 + .0625 + .0625 = 1.0 yes
    # hclen: trailing zeros in ORDER trimmed
    hclen = 19
    while hclen > 4 and cl[ORDER[hclen - 1]] == 0: hclen -= 1
    w.put(hclen - 4, 4)
    for i in range(hclen): w.put(cl[ORDER[i]], 3)
    codes = canon(cl)
    seq = raw_cl_seq if raw_cl_seq is not None else [(l, None) for l in lit + dist]
    for sym, extra in seq:
        w.put_code(codes[sym], cl[sym])
        if sym == 16: w.put(extra, 2)
        elif sym == 17: w.put(extra, 3)
        elif sym == 18: w.put(extra, 7)
    return w, codes

def zstream(w):
    data = w.bytes()
    return b'\x78\x01' + data + b'\x00' * 8

def png_with_stream(z):
    return P.SIG + P.ihdr(2, 2, 8, 2) + P.chunk('IDAT', z) + P.chunk('IEND', b'')

def complete_lit(n=286, end_len=8):

    l = [8]*144 + [9]*112 + [7]*24 + [8]*6
    return l[:n]

        for i in range(l - 1, -1, -1): s.bits.append((code >> i) & 1)

import sys, json, os, zlib, struct
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/media-agent')
from t_cap import lit_code, length_code, EOB
from t_cap3 import stream2
from pic import feed
import pnglib as P
def png_i(z, w, h, depth, ct, inter):
    return P.SIG + P.ihdr(w, h, depth, ct, 0, 0, inter) + P.chunk('IDAT', z) + P.chunk('IEND', b'')
FAR = [length_code(3), ('code', 29, 5), ('bits', 8191, 13)]   # distance 24577+8191
def lits(*bs): return [('lit', b) for b in bs]
def needed(w, h, depth, ch, inter):
    bits = depth * ch
    if not inter:
        return ((w * bits + 7) // 8 + 1) * h
    tot = 0
    for (x0, y0, dx, dy) in [(0,0,8,8),(4,0,8,8),(0,4,4,8),(2,0,4,4),(0,2,2,4),(1,0,2,2),(0,1,1,2)]:
        pw = (w - x0 + dx - 1) // dx if w > x0 else 0
        ph = (h - y0 + dy - 1) // dy if h > y0 else 0
        if pw and ph:
            tot += ((pw * bits + 7) // 8 + 1) * ph
    return tot
for (w, h, depth, ct, inter) in [(17, 8, 4, 0, 1), (6, 1, 8, 0, 0), (17, 8, 4, 0, 0), (8, 8, 8, 0, 1), (3, 3, 8, 2, 1), (33, 20, 8, 6, 1)]:
    ch = P.CHANNELS[ct]
    N = needed(w, h, depth, ch, inter)
    res = []
    for K in range(0, 12):
        data = [7] + [0] * (N - 1 + K)   # first byte: bad filter (7)
        z = stream2([(1, 'fixed', lits(*data) + FAR + [EOB])])
        r = feed(png_i(z, w, h, depth, ct, inter))
        e = r['err']
        res.append('F' if 'filter' in e else ('Z' if 'TooFar' in e else '?'))
    print((w, h, depth, ct, inter), 'N', N, ''.join(res))

from t_cap import lit_code, length_code, EOB
from t_cap3 import stream2
from pic import feed
import pnglib as P
def png_i(z, w, h, depth, ct, inter):
    return P.SIG + P.ihdr(w, h, depth, ct, 0, 0, inter) + P.chunk('IDAT', z) + P.chunk('IEND', b'')
FAR = [length_code(3), ('code', 29, 5), ('bits', 8191, 13)]   # distance 24577+8191
def lits(*bs): return [('lit', b) for b in bs]
def needed(w, h, depth, ch, inter):
    bits = depth * ch
    if not inter:
        return ((w * bits + 7) // 8 + 1) * h
    tot = 0
    for (x0, y0, dx, dy) in [(0,0,8,8),(4,0,8,8),(0,4,4,8),(2,0,4,4),(0,2,2,4),(1,0,2,2),(0,1,1,2)]:
        pw = (w - x0 + dx - 1) // dx if w > x0 else 0
        ph = (h - y0 + dy - 1) // dy if h > y0 else 0
        if pw and ph:
            tot += ((pw * bits + 7) // 8 + 1) * ph
    return tot
for (w, h, depth, ct, inter) in [(17, 8, 4, 0, 1), (6, 1, 8, 0, 0), (17, 8, 4, 0, 0), (8, 8, 8, 0, 1), (3, 3, 8, 2, 1), (33, 20, 8, 6, 1)]:
    ch = P.CHANNELS[ct]

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Run the original (or mine with -m) with a list of commands in a temp dir.
usage: o.py [-m] [-k] [-s] [-e K=V] cmd1 cmd2 ...   (each 'id {json}')
 -s: save project and print selected sections; -k keep dir
"""
import os, sys, subprocess, tempfile, json, shutil
ORIG = '/workspace/executable'
MINE = os.environ.get('MINE', '/workspace/.claude/worktrees/agent-a950f58ddd6484974/target/release/bimcraft-cli')

def run(cmds, exe=ORIG, save=False, env=None, cwd=None, extra=None):
    d = cwd or tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='o')
    args = [exe, 'run']
    for c in cmds:
        args += ['--cmd', c]
    if save:
        args += ['--save', 'x.bimcraft']
    if extra:
        args += extra
    e = dict(os.environ)
    if env:
        e.update(env)
    p = subprocess.run(args, cwd=d, capture_output=True, env=e, timeout=300)
    proj = None
    if save and os.path.exists(os.path.join(d, 'x.bimcraft')):
        proj = json.load(open(os.path.join(d, 'x.bimcraft')))
    if not cwd:
        shutil.rmtree(d)
    return p.returncode, p.stdout.decode('utf-8', 'replace'), p.stderr.decode('utf-8', 'replace'), proj

if __name__ == '__main__':
    a = sys.argv[1:]
    exe = ORIG; save = False; secs = []
    while a and a[0].startswith('-'):
        if a[0] == '-m': exe = MINE; a = a[1:]
        elif a[0] == '-s': save = True; secs = a[1].split(',') if len(a) > 1 else []; a = a[2:]
        else: break
    code, out, err, proj = run(a, exe, save)
    sys.stdout.write(out)
    sys.stdout.write(err)
    print('code', code)
    if proj:
        for s in secs:
            print(s, json.dumps(proj.get(s), ensure_ascii=False)[:3000])

"""Feed picture bytes to the original (or mine) and get the reply/error and decoded pixels."""
import os, sys, json, base64, tempfile, subprocess, shutil
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/media-agent')
from o import run, ORIG, MINE
import pnglib

def feed(data, exe=ORIG, name='p.png', save=True):
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='pic')
    path = os.path.join(d, name)
    open(path, 'wb').write(data)
    c = 'material ' + json.dumps({"name": "G", "texture": {"kind": "image", "path": path}})
    code, out, err, proj = run([c], exe, save=save, cwd=d)
    res = {'code': code, 'out': out.replace(d, '<D>'), 'err': err.replace(d, '<D>')}
    if proj and 'images' in proj:
        imgs = proj['images']
        k = list(imgs)[0]
        png = base64.b64decode(imgs[k]['png'])
        res['id'] = k
        res['png'] = png
        res['name'] = imgs[k]['name']
    shutil.rmtree(d)
    return res

def pixels(res):
    return pnglib.decode_stored(res['png'])

class BR:
    def __init__(s,d): s.d=d; s.pos=0
    def bit(s):
        b=(s.d[s.pos>>3]>>(s.pos&7))&1; s.pos+=1; return b
    def bits(s,n):
        v=0
        for i in range(n): v|=s.bit()<<i
        return v

print('bfinal',bfinal,'btype',btype)

def build(lengths):
    # canonical codes
    maxl=max(lengths)
    bl_count=[0]*(maxl+1)
    for l in lengths:
        if l: bl_count[l]+=1
    code=0; next_code=[0]*(maxl+2)

    codes={}
    for n,l in enumerate(lengths):
        if l:
            codes[(l,next_code[l])]=n; next_code[l]+=1

from pic import feed, pixels
import pnglib as P
random.seed(11)
def box(src, w, h):
    nw, nh = max(1, w//2), max(1, h//2)
    out = []
    for y in range(nh):
        row = []
        for x in range(nw):
            q = [src[min(2*y+dy, h-1)][min(2*x+dx, w-1)] for dy in (0,1) for dx in (0,1)]
            row.append(tuple((sum(p[c] for p in q)+2)//4 for c in range(3)) + (255,))
        out.append(row)
    return out, nw, nh
for (w,h) in [(1,2000),(3,2000),(2050,5),(4100,3)]:
    px = [[(random.randrange(256),random.randrange(256),random.randrange(256)) for x in range(w)] for y in range(h)]
    r = feed(P.make_png(w,h,px))
    W,H,rows = pixels(r)
    # model: iterative halving
    cur, cw, ch = [[p+(255,) for p in row] for row in px], w, h
    while cw > 1024 or ch > 1024:
        cur, cw, ch = box(cur, cw, ch)
    ok = (cw,ch)==(W,H) and all(tuple(cur[y][x])==tuple(rows[y][x]) for y in range(H) for x in range(W))
    # model 2: one-step box of 2^k
    print((w,h), '->', (W,H), 'iterative model', ok)

import sys, zlib, struct
sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp/media-agent')
from pic import feed, pixels
import pnglib as P
SIG = P.SIG
def mk(*chunks):
    return SIG + b''.join(chunks)
IE = P.chunk('IEND', b'')
IHP = P.ihdr(2,2,8,3)
raw_pal = b'\x00\x00\x01\x00\x02\x01'
IH = P.ihdr(2,2,8,2)
bad_raw = b'\x07' + bytes(6) + b'\x00' + bytes(6)
def stored(data, final=1):
    n = len(data)
    return bytes([final, n & 255, n >> 8, (~n)&255, ((~n)>>8)&255]) + data
cases = {
 'bad plte + bad zlib': mk(IHP, P.chunk('PLTE', bytes(4)), P.chunk('IDAT', b'\x78\x9c\xff\xff'), IE),
 'bad plte + bad crc idat': mk(IHP, P.chunk('PLTE', bytes(4)), P.chunk('IDAT', zlib.compress(raw_pal), crc=1), IE),
 'bad plte + bad filter': mk(IHP, P.chunk('PLTE', bytes(4)), P.chunk('IDAT', zlib.compress(b'\x07\x00\x01\x00\x02\x01')), IE),
 'bad plte + no rows': mk(IHP, P.chunk('PLTE', bytes(4)), P.chunk('IDAT', zlib.compress(b'')), IE),
 'bad plte + short stream': mk(IHP, P.chunk('PLTE', bytes(4)), P.chunk('IDAT', zlib.compress(raw_pal)[:5]), IE),
 'bad filter + bad crc': mk(IH, P.chunk('IDAT', zlib.compress(bad_raw), crc=1), IE),
 'bad filter + truncated stream': mk(IH, P.chunk('IDAT', zlib.compress(bad_raw)[:-6]), IE),
 'bad filter row2 + truncated in row2': mk(IH, P.chunk('IDAT', b'\x78\x01' + stored(b'\x00' + bytes(6) + b'\x07' + bytes(6), 0)), IE),
 'bad filter row1 in 2nd idat + bad crc 1st': mk(IH, P.chunk('IDAT', b'\x78\x01' + stored(b'\x00' + bytes(6), 0), crc=1), P.chunk('IDAT', stored(b'\x07' + bytes(6))), IE),
 'bad filter row0 in 1st idat, bad zlib in 2nd': mk(IH, P.chunk('IDAT', b'\x78\x01' + stored(b'\x07' + bytes(6), 0)), P.chunk('IDAT', b'\xff\xff\xff'), IE),
 'bad filter + eof in idat': SIG + IH + P.chunk('IDAT', zlib.compress(bad_raw))[:-6],
 'bad plte + eof': SIG + IHP + P.chunk('PLTE', bytes(4)) + P.chunk('IDAT', zlib.compress(raw_pal))[:-6],
 'bad plte + no idat': mk(IHP, P.chunk('PLTE', bytes(4)), IE),
}
names = sys.argv[1:] or list(cases)

    r = feed(cases[n])
    print('%-45s' % n, r['code'], r['err'].strip().replace('line 1 (material): material: <D>/p.png: ','').replace('\n', ' // ')[:300])

import pnglib as P

class BW:
    def __init__(s): s.bits = []
    def put(s, v, n):
        for i in range(n): s.bits.append((v >> i) & 1)
    def put_code(s, code, l):  # huffman codes are MSB first
        for i in range(l - 1, -1, -1): s.bits.append((code >> i) & 1)
    def bytes(s):
        out = bytearray()
        for i in range(0, len(s.bits), 8):
            b = 0
            for j, bit in enumerate(s.bits[i:i+8]): b |= bit << j
            out.append(b)
        return bytes(out)

def canon(lengths):
    maxl = max(lengths) if any(lengths) else 0
    bl = [0]*(maxl+1)
    for l in lengths:
        if l: bl[l] += 1
    code = 0; nxt = [0]*(maxl+2)
    for b in range(1, maxl+1):
        code = (code + bl[b-1]) << 1
        nxt[b] = code
    codes = [0]*len(lengths)
    for n, l in enumerate(lengths):
        if l: codes[n] = nxt[l]; nxt[l] += 1
    return codes

    """lit: list of hlit lengths, dist: list of hdist lengths. cl: code length code lengths (19)"""
    w = BW()
    w.put(final, 1); w.put(2, 2)
    hlit = len(lit); hdist = len(dist)
    w.put(hlit - 257, 5); w.put(hdist - 1, 5)

        cl = [4]*12 + [5]*4 + [4, 5, 5]  # .75 + .125 + .0625 + .0625 = 1.0 yes
    # hclen: trailing zeros in ORDER trimmed

W = 6
def run(name, blocks, adler=True):
    z = stream(blocks, adler=adler)

    from dyn import BW
    w = BW()
    for final, kind, syms in blocks:

import sys, json, os, zlib, struct
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/media-agent')
from t_cap import lit_code, length_code, EOB
from t_cap3 import stream2
from pic import feed
import pnglib as P
def png_i(z, w, h, depth, ct, inter):
    return P.SIG + P.ihdr(w, h, depth, ct, 0, 0, inter) + P.chunk('IDAT', z) + P.chunk('IEND', b'')
FAR = [length_code(3), ('code', 29, 5), ('bits', 8191, 13)]   # distance 24577+8191
def lits(*bs): return [('lit', b) for b in bs]
def needed(w, h, depth, ch, inter):
    bits = depth * ch
    if not inter:
        return ((w * bits + 7) // 8 + 1) * h
    tot = 0
    for (x0, y0, dx, dy) in [(0,0,8,8),(4,0,8,8),(0,4,4,8),(2,0,4,4),(0,2,2,4),(1,0,2,2),(0,1,1,2)]:
        pw = (w - x0 + dx - 1) // dx if w > x0 else 0
        ph = (h - y0 + dy - 1) // dy if h > y0 else 0
        if pw and ph:
            tot += ((pw * bits + 7) // 8 + 1) * ph
    return tot
for (w, h, depth, ct, inter) in [(17, 8, 4, 0, 1), (6, 1, 8, 0, 0), (17, 8, 4, 0, 0), (8, 8, 8, 0, 1), (3, 3, 8, 2, 1), (33, 20, 8, 6, 1)]:
    ch = P.CHANNELS[ct]
    N = needed(w, h, depth, ch, inter)
    res = []
    for K in range(0, 12):
        data = [7] + [0] * (N - 1 + K)   # first byte: bad filter (7)
        z = stream2([(1, 'fixed', lits(*data) + FAR + [EOB])])
        r = feed(png_i(z, w, h, depth, ct, inter))
        e = r['err']
        res.append('F' if 'filter' in e else ('Z' if 'TooFar' in e else '?'))
    print((w, h, depth, ct, inter), 'N', N, ''.join(res))

    def zeros_until(n):
        nonlocal out
        if out == 0 and n > 0:
            bw.put_code(*lit_code(0)); out = 1
        while out + 258 <= n:

def huff_table(bits, vals):
    codes = {}
    code = 0
    k = 0
    for l in range(1, 17):
        for _ in range(bits[l - 1]):
            codes[vals[k]] = (code, l)
            code += 1
            k += 1
        code <<= 1
    return codes

def fdct(block):
    # straightforward float DCT-II
    out = [0.0] * 64
    for v in range(8):
        for u in range(8):
            s = 0.0
            for y in range(8):
                for x in range(8):
                    s += block[y * 8 + x] * math.cos((2 * x + 1) * u * math.pi / 16) * math.cos((2 * y + 1) * v * math.pi / 16)
            cu = 1 / math.sqrt(2) if u == 0 else 1
            cv = 1 / math.sqrt(2) if v == 0 else 1
            out[v * 8 + u] = 0.25 * cu * cv * s
    return out

class BitWriter:
    def __init__(self):
        self.out = bytearray()
        self.acc = 0
        self.nbits = 0
    def put(self, code, length):
        for i in range(length - 1, -1, -1):
            self.acc = (self.acc << 1) | ((code >> i) & 1)
            self.nbits += 1
            if self.nbits == 8:
                self.out.append(self.acc)
                if self.acc == 0xff:
                    self.out.append(0)
                self.acc = 0
                self.nbits = 0
    def flush(self):
        if self.nbits > 0:
            self.acc <<= (8 - self.nbits)
            self.acc |= (1 << (8 - self.nbits)) - 1
            self.out.append(self.acc)
            if self.acc == 0xff:
                self.out.append(0)
            self.acc = 0
            self.nbits = 0

def magnitude(v):
    if v == 0:
        return 0, 0, 0
    a = abs(v)
    s = a.bit_length()
    if v < 0:
        v = v - 1  # ones complement for negatives
    return s, v & ((1 << s) - 1), s

def encode_block(bw, coef, dc_prev, dc_codes, ac_codes):
    dc = coef[0] - dc_prev
    s, bits, _ = magnitude(dc)
    bw.put(*dc_codes[s])
    if s:
        bw.put(bits, s)
    run = 0
    for k in range(1, 64):
        c = coef[ZIGZAG[k]]
        if c == 0:
            run += 1
        else:
            while run > 15:
                bw.put(*ac_codes[0xf0])
                run -= 16
            s, bits, _ = magnitude(c)
            bw.put(*ac_codes[(run << 4) | s])
            bw.put(bits, s)
            run = 0
    if run > 0:
        bw.put(*ac_codes[0x00])
    return coef[0]

def quantize(dct, qt):
    return [int(round(dct[i] / qt[i])) for i in range(64)]

def rgb_to_ycbcr(r, g, b):
    y = 0.299 * r + 0.587 * g + 0.114 * b
    cb = -0.168736 * r - 0.331264 * g + 0.5 * b + 128
    cr = 0.5 * r - 0.418688 * g - 0.081312 * b + 128
    return y, cb, cr

def encode(w, h, pixels, subsample=(1, 1), qlum=None, qchr=None, gray=False, restart=0):
    """pixels: list of (r,g,b) rows (or grayscale ints if gray). subsample: (hx,hy) for chroma -> 4:2:0 is (2,2)."""
    qlum = qlum or STD_LUM
    qchr = qchr or STD_CHR

    out += b'\xff\xdb' + struct.pack('>H', 2 + 65) + b'\x00' + bytes(qlum[ZIGZAG[i]] for i in range(64))
    if not gray:
        out += b'\xff\xdb' + struct.pack('>H', 2 + 65) + b'\x01' + bytes(qchr[ZIGZAG[i]] for i in range(64))
    # SOF0

    else:

    sof = struct.pack('>BHHB', 8, h, w, len(comps))
    for (cid, hx, hy, tq) in comps:
        sof += struct.pack('>BBB', cid, (hx << 4) | hy, tq)
    out += b'\xff\xc0' + struct.pack('>H', 2 + len(sof)) + sof

        body = struct.pack('>B', (cls << 4) | tid) + bytes(bits) + bytes(vals)
        return b'\xff\xc4' + struct.pack('>H', 2 + len(body)) + body

    out += dht(1, 0, AC_LUM_BITS, AC_LUM_VALS)
    if not gray:
        out += dht(0, 1, DC_CHR_BITS, DC_CHR_VALS)
        out += dht(1, 1, AC_CHR_BITS, AC_CHR_VALS)
    if restart:
        out += b'\xff\xdd' + struct.pack('>HH', 4, restart)
    dc_lum = huff_table(DC_LUM_BITS, DC_LUM_VALS)
    ac_lum = huff_table(AC_LUM_BITS, AC_LUM_VALS)
    dc_chr = huff_table(DC_CHR_BITS, DC_CHR_VALS)
    ac_chr = huff_table(AC_CHR_BITS, AC_CHR_VALS)
    # SOS
    if gray:
        sos = struct.pack('>B', 1) + struct.pack('>BB', 1, 0x00) + b'\x00\x3f\x00'
    else:
        sos = struct.pack('>B', 3) + struct.pack('>BB', 1, 0x00) + struct.pack('>BB', 2, 0x11) + struct.pack('>BB', 3, 0x11) + b'\x00\x3f\x00'
    out += b'\xff\xda' + struct.pack('>H', 2 + len(sos)) + sos

        return plane[yy * pw + xx]

        Cr = {}

        cbs = [[0.0] * w for _ in range(h)]
        crs = [[0.0] * w for _ in range(h)]
        for y in range(h):

                ys[y][x] = yy
                cbs[y][x] = cb
                crs[y][x] = cr
        # chroma subsampled dimensions
        cw = (w + hx - 1) // hx
        ch = (h + hy - 1) // hy
        cbp = [[0.0] * cw for _ in range(ch)]
        crp = [[0.0] * cw for _ in range(ch)]
        for cy in range(ch):
            for cx in range(cw):
                acc_cb = acc_cr = n = 0
                for dy in range(hy):
                    for dx in range(hx):
                        sx = min(cx * hx + dx, w - 1)
                        sy = min(cy * hy + dy, h - 1)
                        acc_cb += cbs[sy][sx]
                        acc_cr += crs[sy][sx]
                        n += 1
                cbp[cy][cx] = acc_cb / n
                crp[cy][cx] = acc_cr / n
        planes = {1: (ys, w, h, hx, hy), 2: (cbp, cw, ch, 1, 1), 3: (crp, crw if False else cw, ch, 1, 1)}
        order = [1, 2, 3]
    bw = BitWriter()
    Hmax = max(c[1] for c in comps)
    Vmax = max(c[2] for c in comps)
    mcux = (w + 8 * Hmax - 1) // (8 * Hmax)
    mcuy = (h + 8 * Vmax - 1) // (8 * Vmax)
    dc_prev = {cid: 0 for cid, _, _, _ in comps}
    qtl = {0: qlum, 1: qchr}
    dctab = {0: dc_lum, 1: dc_chr}
    actab = {0: ac_lum, 1: ac_chr}
    mcu_count = 0
    for my in range(mcuy):

                bw.flush()
                rst = 0xd0 + ((mcu_count // restart - 1) % 8)
                bw.out.append(0xff)
                bw.out.append(rst)
                dc_prev = {cid: 0 for cid, _, _, _ in comps}
            for (cid, chx, chy, tq) in comps:
                if gray:
                    plane = pixels; pw = w; ph = h
                else:
                    plane, pw, ph, _, _ = planes[cid]
                for by in range(chy):
                    for bx in range(chx):
                        block = [0.0] * 64
                        for yy in range(8):
                            for xx in range(8):

                                py = (my * chy + by) * 8 + yy

                                else:
                                    val = plane[py][px]
                                block[yy * 8 + xx] = val - 128

                        qt = qtl[tq]
                        coef = quantize(dct, qt)
                        dc_prev[cid] = encode_block(bw, coef, dc_prev[cid], dctab[tq if False else (0 if cid == 1 else 1)], actab[0 if cid == 1 else 1])

    bw.flush()
    out += bytes(bw.out)
    out += b'\xff\xd9'
    return bytes(out)

I've completed the implementation. Here is my final report.

## Branch & commits
- Branch: `worktree-agent-a950f58ddd6484974`, head `97616da` (6 commits).
- All code is in `src/media/` (10 files, ~4150 lines). One minimal edit outside it: `src/commands/mod.rs::always_step` now delegates to `media::always_step` (needed because the original makes an undo step for `material`/`paint` even when the model is unchanged).

## What matches (verified against the original with `/tmp/tools/cmp.py` and thousands of generated cases)
- **`material`** — create/change/rename/delete; `#rrggbb` and `[r,g,b]` colours; transparency; cut/surface built-in patterns and fill-pattern names (stored as `cut_pattern`/`surface_pattern` GUIDs); textures by kind and by picture (`path`/`image`); `null`; every error text and the exact validation order (including the subtle rule that an omitted texture `kind` is inherited from the material's current texture, so "needs a kind" only fires when there is none, and that texture errors precede colour/transparency/pattern errors). Delete refused when a layer/family/paint uses it, with the original's messages. 600+ random-sequence fuzz cases pass; remaining diffs in my `material` suite are only from sibling commands I don't own (`type`, `wall`).
- **Pictures (PNG)** — decode of all colour types, bit depths, palettes, transparency, interlacing; the stored 8-bit-RGBA PNG is **byte-identical** (fdeflate Sub-filter packing, stored-block fallback, `78 01` header) and the `img-` FNV-1a id matches; the 16-million-pixel limit and iterative 2×2-box halving to ≤1024px. ~2600 valid+corrupt PNG fuzz cases pass, including the png-crate error texts (`CRC error…`, `Corrupt deflate stream. <fdeflate variant>`, chunk-ordering, the palette-overflow **panic** reproduced verbatim) and the png-crate's progressive output-cap error ordering.
- **`favorite`** — list/save/load/delete for materials (with their pictures) and families; exact `favorites.json` bytes (`version 1`, pretty-printed, sorted); `BIMCRAFT_FAVORITES`/XDG/`~/.config`/`path` precedence; and the serde error texts for malformed files (`invalid type…`, `missing field…`, `unknown field…`, line/column) — 1200 material-favorite fuzz files pass.
- **`library`** — `library`/`parts` listing with `kind`/`name` filters, ids/GUIDs, and `parts` (layers/forms/symbols/connectors) in id order, matching exactly.
- **`paint`** — all faces, `id`/`ids`, GUID refs, `null` removal, every error; 48/48.

## What doesn't match, and why
- **JPEG non-flat pixels**: baseline decoding uses an stb-derived integer IDCT, but zune-jpeg's IDCT differs by a rare ±1 in some AC-bearing pixels (a specific rounding I could not reproduce without reading its source, which is disallowed). Flat/DC-only images are exact — so the two test assets `gray.jpg` and `mono.jpg` decode correctly and produce the right id — but most non-flat JPEGs differ by ±1, which changes the stored-PNG id. JPEG error texts largely match (27/29 of my cases).
- **Progressive JPEG (SOF2)**: zune decodes it; my build returns an error. Not implemented.
- **Family `favorite` load**: materials-with-pictures round-trip and the file bytes/listing match, but on *load* the original re-allocates fresh ids/GUIDs for the family's forms/symbols (counting down), whereas I keep the stored ones; this part-id reallocation belongs to the family module's conventions (families are the "later" item in the spec).

## What the core must provide
- **`inspect` is a stub** (`src/inspect.rs` shows only counts/history/language/levels/name). The original's `inspect` must additionally show, sorted: `materials` (each as the `material` reply shows it — patterns and pictures resolved to names), `images` (`{id: {name, size: [w,h]}}`), plus `types`, `families`, and the other sections. I've left ready-to-call helpers `media::material::inspect_materials(pr)` and `inspect_images(pr)` that produce the exact material/image shapes. `TOP_ORDER`'s placement of `images` (right after `materials`) is already correct.
- The `always_step` delegation I added should be kept (or the equivalent mechanism preserved) so `material`/`paint` always create an undo step.
